Secondary containment was being utilized to manage regulated substances and waste as per regulation and appeared to be functioning as designed. Operator immediately addressed the situation by vacuuming up the affected area, cleaning the extension cord and placing it inside of secondary containment. Operator actions appear to have successfully remediated the affected area. No other violations were observed during the inspection.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/22/2026 to REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC in Liberty Township, Tioga county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/22/2026
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8278993
Permit API: 117-22299
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/22/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that an estimated 5 gallons of produced fluid was released through a hole in a section of secondary containment. It rained heavily during this inspection. Six wells have been drilled and stimulated on the well pad. It appears that flowback operations are complete. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition.A battery of frac tanks is present within secondary containment near the production tanks. The tanks and secondary containment appear to be in good condition. No holes or patches were observed in the containment liner. The containment appeared to be retaining water. The fluid within the containment had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 947 uS/cm. The puddles on the pad surface near the containment had an EC of less than 900 uS/cm. A bucket within the secondary containment had a label on it which says spill waste for disposal. In one corner of the containment, the fluid in the containment had a petroleum sheen on it. A water truck driver arrived during this inspection and began to vacuum out the containment during this inspection. In a phone call with Brett Staller of Repsol, he stated that a water truck driver had dropped a hose on the secondary containment liner for the frac tank battery and created a 4-6 inch hole in the containment. Pad material was excavated beneath the hole and the hole was patched, he stated. I could not see a hole or patch in the liner during this inspection but there was approximately 2 inches of stormwater in the containment at the time due to the heavy rain. The bottom of the liner was also obscured where a petroleum sheen was present on the surface of the stormwater in the southeast corner of the containment. Violations cited and are considered immediately corrected.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/03/2023 to BIG DOG ENERGY LLC in Hempfield Twp, Westmoreland county. 78a64a(b) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – All regulated substances, including solid wastes and other regulated substances in equipment or vehicles, failed to be managed within secondary containment on the well site.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BIG DOG ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/03/2023
Violation Code: 78a64a(b) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – All regulated substances, including solid wastes and other regulated substances in equipment or vehicles, failed to be managed within secondary containment on the well site.
Violation ID: 981092
Permit API: 129-25570
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Hempfield Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/03/2023
Comments: On January 3, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection on the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3435475 where violations were outstanding due to a missing Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plans, and no NOV response received from the operator. Also, no production reports had been submitted since 2014 per Department database, at the time of that inspection.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign was present at the well site entrance (see photo 1). No Emergency Response plans, or other required documents were onsite. No evidence of leaks or discharge could be found around the new production tanks, and they appeared to be sound at the time of inspection. However, they were not equipped with secondary containment (see photos 3 and 8). Soil conductivity readings were taken in the earthen berms surrounding these tanks, and at the bases of these tanks (see photos 4-7). The well tag and required operator's information was present on the meter box (see photo 8). The Additional piping and production equipment was left onsite. Some tire rutting was observed at the back of the well site looking from the road, which could be due to third party traversing (see photo 10). The ground overall was soft, which could lead to future stabilization concerns. Therefore, the Department recommends that the operator take additional stabilization measures to prevent any potential E and S issues from developing.Based on observations from today's inspection, the violations that were continued in IR 3435475 shall remain outstanding, since no changes were made since and no NOV response has been received to date. An additional violation shall be issued against the production tanks, since they are not equipped with secondary containment in an unconventional site.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/18/2025 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Charleston Township, Tioga county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/18/2025
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8249811
Permit API: 117-20505
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Charleston Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/18/2025
Comments: On 9/18/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a follow-up incident inspection in response to complaint #389073 at the Seneca Vandergrift 290 well site located in Charleston Twp, Tioga Co. It was 46 degrees and mostly cloudy when I arrived on site. Rainfall has not impacted the region in the last 48 hours.There are four active wells on site staged for production along with two that are in the process of being plugged. The Vandergrift 290 2H and 5H wells have had recent plugging operation and a plugged well monument has been installed on the 2H well, plugged date 12/4/2024. The area that was excavated around and north of the well cellars remains open along with the areas on the fill slope and across the grassy field north of the pad. Elevated conductance above 4000 uS was found in soils in the bottoms of the 2H, 3H, 5H, and 6H well cellars. The highest reading found in the 4H well cellar was 1385 uS conductance in the soil and 1035 uS conductance in the water. The highest reading witnessed in the 1H well cellar was 1230 uS conductance. Elevated conductance readings were also found at the north edge of the pad, above the east and west excavated areas of the fill slope. I did witness a wet area of soil 10 feet up from the base of the fill slope and within the approximate center of the west excavated area that field tested above 4000 uS conductance. Liquid flowing down through the excavated area below the fill slope and into the catch basin sump field tested at 1229 microsiemens conductance. Liquid in the sump field tested at 1481 microsiemens conductance and liquid flowing out of the sump field tested at 1693 microsiemens conductance.Temporary compost filter socks that were installed at the base of the fill slope and in the excavated area of the field on the north side of the location that do have sediments above 50% of the height of the sock. Temporary stabilization that has been applied to the fill slope and the excavated area of the field needs to be refreshed. Comments: On May 15, 2025, an inspection was conducted on the Hillview Cemetery 2 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3954937, where violations issued from IR 3872789 were left outstanding against the severe rutting that remained onsite and for failure to post the API number and operator's information onsite.Prior to the time of IR 3954937 on March 3, 2025, Apollo Resources representative Jesse Colangelo sent an email to the Department, stating that the operator "will fix the road as soon as the weather gets better its a little wet now" and will "put a sticker on it this week", in response to the lack of API number and operator's information posted onsite.The following was observed:The areas of significant rutting that have been observed in the access road and well site remain (see photos 1-4 and 6). The most severely rutted portion in the access road is situated approximately 100 feet from slate Creek, and therefore may continue to pose the potential to threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth (see photo 5). No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the well head (see photo 7). The brine tank appears to have been reconnected to the well equipment (see photos 8 and 11). No evidence of leaks or distressed vegetation was observed where the brine tank line is located. The brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection, with no staining or distressed vegetation on the ground around it (see photos 10 and 12). The API number and a means to identify and/or contact the operator have not been posted onsite since the time of IR 3954937 (see photo 13).Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued from IR 3872789 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: On April 17, 2025 the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Mountain View LTV 2 well located in Rostraver Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3715546 where violations were issued for a release and for IR 3882155 where violations were continued due to site conditions being unchanged. The LTV 2 site is located within abandoned coal mine land and therefore the well site is composed of coal refuge. Mountain View Operator Dave Lindahl informed the Department via email (documented in IR 3797419) that this abandoned coal mine land is to be remediated by the Department's Clean Streams Program and that this well site is included in their remediationplans. Mr. Lindahl also stated that what the Department observes to be a release from production equipment at the well site's entrance is actually runoff from the spoil piles upslope of the well site.During IR 3882155, the Department observed the spoil piles Mr. Lindahl mentioned, however, the Department did not observe any evidence of erosion channels or a distinct pathway that goes from the spoil piles and leads to the entrance of the well site where the release is observed to be. A distinct change in the ground level is observed in the release arearight next to the wellhead and separator piping, which further supports the notion that fluid from this production equipment is where the release originated. This in conjunction with elevated soil conductivity readings in this area lead the Department in IR 3715546 to again recommend the Operator remediate the release in accordance with the Department's policy for small spills despite the Clean Streams Program's remediation site plans including the LTV 2 site within it.At the time of this inspection, site conditions appeared to be unchanged. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it and a production tank was observed to be lopsided and sinking into the ground. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near any of the production equipment on site, however, the spill area documented in IR 3715546 still appears to be present. Fluid is observed to be pooled starting at the wellhead and proceeding to exit the well site and flow downslope. Report Details

Violation ID: 863493
Permit API: 115-22557
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Auburn Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-09-17
Comments: The Department was on-site in response to the report of a spill incident of more than (5) gallons of diesel based drilling mud that occurred on 9/16/19 at 17:05 hours. The weather conditions are sunny skies with a light breeze, and temperatures in the upper 60's. Remediation of the impacted area affiliated with the spill was in progress. Resource Environmental of Montrose, PA is the Cabot subcontractor delineating the extent of the impact via the use of a photoionization detector (PID) meter to determine the presence of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds. H&P Flex Rig 259 is the drilling rig on the location. The current drilling depth of the M Powers 12H well is (4,351.59) feet. Cassidy Moyer, DEP WQS and I initially met with Mike Stansfield, Drilling Engineer of Cabot in the site office/company man trailer. Mr. Stansfield provided the following information relevant to site activities and the spill incident. "The rig is on the M Powers 12H well. Remediation of this well is in progress. The 4H and 8H wells will be drilled to total depth (TD). All other wells on the pad have been drilled to TD. A low cement top was found when a cement bond log was run. Perforations were shot in the production casing at (4,430) and (6,000) feet. Cement was pumped into the production casing and through the cement retainer. The cement retainer didn't hold in the production casing. The cement retainer was drilled out. Diesel based drilling mud overflowed the 12H well casing vent tank onto containment. Some of the mud got outside the containment. The mud came out of the top of the tank in the form of a flow, then rolled off the containment to the pad surface, and then it flowed under the containment. The spill volume is over (5) gallons, but may be under (42). We may be able to calculate the volume of the spill, and determine it is under (42) gallons. The spill happened around 5 PM yesterday. Marlon Droddy, the site company man found the spill and reported it to Mike Cromley, the site safety man. Remediation of the impacted area started last night. Initially, we were not able to dig under the vent lines. We eventually moved the vent tanks and the containment to evaluate the extent of the impact.” Resource Environmental provided the following information relevant to remediation of the impacted area. “We arrived here today at 9AM. Comments: On 1/14/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 20 degrees and mostly cloudy when I arrived on location. Snow was scattered across the location. While inspecting the original Taft 851 1V pad, I met Seneca's Ian Thom who described upcoming operations as follows: A vent pipe sticking from the ground and connected to the well casing may have been jarred during construction activities, causing the well to start bubbling. A Plants and Goodwin well servicing rig is mobilizing to the site to pump cement downhole. A secondary containment structure has been installed around the wellhead and two frac tanks remain on site, staged in secondary containment.I met Seneca's Jim Westfield on the north pad who described current operations as follows: The five newly drilled and completed wells are staged for flow-back. Two sand separators were attached to each wellhead. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs have been installed on site, all staged in secondary containment. Six frac tanks were staged north of the wellheads for flowback operations. Secondary containment remains installed around the wellheads.28 frac tanks were staged in secondary containment on the west side of the location. Jim was unsure if these would be left on site for the next round of drilling and completion.Vegetation is established in recently constructed areas. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Infiltration berm 3 and the sedimentation basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Due to frozen conditions during this inspection, conductivity readings were not taken. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. Continue to determine the cause of elevated conductance discovered during previous inspections to prevent future occurrences. Remove the elevated conductance fluids and contaminated soils from the pad surface and the sediment basin.2. Continuously monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered.I left the site at 1525 hours.

Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of produced fluid. The release occurred at the frac tanks near the wells just to the northwest of the wells. At the time of inspection, the quantity of released produced fluid was unknown but was reported to be at least 1 barrel. I met onsite with Mike Deming, Expand. There were two sets of containment, each approximately 70' long by 55' wide. The staining appeared to be concentrated near the front-center of the tanks and between the two sets of containment for about half the length of the tanks. There were some holes identified in the offload area of the secondary containment shown in Photo 3. Soil conductivity was checked using a Groline soil conductivity meter. The damp areas/fluid were greater than 4.00 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm) which is the upper limit of the conductivity meter. Expand indicated that the conductivity of a few puddles in these areas was around 21 mS/cm, having used a YSI meter. There were no other puddles on the pad surface or seeps found between the pad and the infiltration basins. The soil conductivity below the pad and in the basins ranged between 0.05 mS/cm and 0.68 mS/cm.The set of tanks in the foreground of Photo 1 are going to be cleaned and removed in order to pull the containment. Some of the tanks in the background of Photo 1 will also be removed and the containment lifted as much as possible to facilitate a full assessment and remediation of the impacted area. The remediation is tentatively scheduled to begin 7/9/25.Per a discussion with Mike Deming, the site will be remediated under Act 2 requirements. The result of this inspection is Violations noted for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a). There are also outstanding violations for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a) due to a release documented in inspection 3981577 from 5/20/25 and inspection 3982600 from 5/22/25. The release detailed in those inspections is also undergoing Act 2 remediation. The violations may be closed after the completion of Act 2 remediation.

Comments: On 02/03/2025 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 0915 hours, weather was 33F and cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).All standing water observed on the pad surface was frozen solid.There are 2 recently drilled wells located onsite which are currently undergoing flow back as a result of the completion of hydraulic fracturing activities; well permits are posted with the Act 9 sign at the site entrance (photos #1 and 2). 2 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #3). The GPUs are not yet in use but are held in a secondary containment structure. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #4); the tanks are not yet labeled, and I discussed the need to label them with personnel onsite; they informed me that they would be labeled after they dried off. Two modular aboveground storage structures (MASS's) are located onsite to hold brine during flow back, and a lined residual waste container is located next to them and held on containment (photo #5). Multiple upright brine and temporary storage tanks for holding produced fluids during flow back are also noted onsite; all tanks are held in secondary containment which appears to be functioning as intended (photos #6 and 7).Site stabilization could not be adequately assessed due to snow coverage. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. A weekly erosion and sediment (E and S) inspection log is available for review at the site entrance and is up to date (photo #8). One infiltration basin serve as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) controls (photo #9). No standing water was observed in the PCSM control it appears to be functioning as intended.The violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962.No violations noted. I departed the site at 1015 hours.

Violation ID: 8268637
Permit API: 059-25309
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Center Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/25/2026
Comments: On 03/25/26 an incident inspection of the GH2 Well Site was conducted in response to the report of a spill received by the Department on 03/25/26. (CTS #396140) Background:On 03/25/26 CNX self-reported a release of production fluid. On 03/25/26 I spoke to Bruce Carpenter of CNX to acquire additional details about the spill. Mr. Carpenter informed me the spill was the result of a leaking pipe union that carried produced fluid to the bulk tanks and that the approximate volume of the spill was estimated to be roughly 20 gallons. Findings:-An act 9 sign was present at the entrance to site (Photo #1). -The spill originated from a leaking pipe union outside of the containment berm of the production tanks (Photos #4).-Remediation was underway in the area of the spill (Photo #2-3).-Elevated conductivity was observed around the excavated area (Photo #5-6). -No elevated conductivity was observed outside of the spill area (Photos #7-9).-A rolloff box was present on site for the impacted materials (Photo #10). No impacts to WoC were observed. Violations of 78a57(a), SWMA 301, 91.34(a), and 78a54 are being issued for the release of brine to the ground.

Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8246612

Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/28/2025
Comments: Incident Inspection of Expand's "Cahill" Marcellus well site.Steve Moyer (Expand) called the DEP yesterday (August 27, 2025) to report they discovered an underground flow line leaked an unknown quantity of produced liquid.I spoke with Mike Deming (Expand) on site during this inspection who explained their Forward Looking Infrared (FLIR) camera technician discovered natural gas emitting from the pad surface on Friday August 22, 2025 during a quarterly inspection. On Monday August 25, 2025 Expand pressurized all 3 Marcellus wells with natural gas. The 2H Marcellus well lost approximately 500 psi over 20 minutes, indicating the leak. On Wednesday August 27, 2025 they pressurized the 2H well with air to locate the production line leaks more accurately. Expand checked the fill slope for signs of seepage, and did not see any liquid or stressed vegetation.I spoke with Andy Senefelder (Crescent Environmental, P.G.) on site who explained that yesterday an excavator dug a ~3' deep x ~90' long trench above the production lines. Then they hand dug 9 test pits ("potholes") in the pea gravel surrounding the production line to find the extent of the leaks. Liquid in the potholes returned electrical conductivity (EC) readings of 23-106 mS/cm. Crescent tested the pad material removed for the trench which returned EC readings of 0.05-0.45 mS/cm, indicating the material above the line is not impacted. So far, a vac truck has removed approximately 2 barrels of liquid from sumps in the trench. Demming calculated the approximate maximum amount of liquid released is 21.5 barrels.Expand removed the 2 sections of 4" diameter line that leaked, and are testing the metal to determine a cause of the pinholes in it. They plan to replace all of the production lines between the wells and the GPUs with above ground pipe.After the old lines are removed, Crescent plans to sample in compliance with Act 2 Cleanup standards.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion orsedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Runoff water flows to basins on the east and south ends of the site.Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles on the east end of the pad surface has EC of 0.30-0.55 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5. I did not see any other puddles on the pad.Violations for the production liquid release are cited to the 2H well permit.Air temp 54FJLP

Inspection Date: 5/18/2026
Comments: On 5/18/2026, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill at the Mazure William well pad in Hanover Township, Washington County. The spill was reportedly discovered on 5/17/2026, at 6:20 AM; and reported to the Department on 5/17/2026, at 8:05 AM. The spill was reportedly caused by a pipe fitting failure on the flash separator unit. An estimated 15 gallons of a produced water/condensate mixture released to the surface of the well pad. Accompanying the Department during this inspection is Range Resources representative Nick Reda. An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP-2) for this site was terminated on 9/02/2020.The following was observed during the inspection:The flash separator unit has been disconnected and moved to accommodate remediation operations (photos 4 and 5). An excavation that appears to be approximately 10 feet by 15 feet was observed where the spill reportedly occurred (photo 3). Reda stated that approximately 98% of the impacted material has been removed at the time of this inspection, with the only remaining impacted material being located around a compressed air line. Completing remediation will reportedly require the use of hand tools to avoid damaging the compressed air line. No visual impacts, such as residual staining, were observed where remediation has been completed. The Department recommends that the operator assess the area underneath the disconnected flash separator unit for potential drips and remediate as necessary, in accordance with current regulations. Three rolloff foxes containing impacted material were observed at the southeastern corner of the well pad (photo 10).The access road appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photo 2). Excavations are being conducted at the well to remediate the spill (photos 3 and 9). No concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation were noted at the well pad during this inspection.The GPU/Vertical Separator Units are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photos 7). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022. The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection (photo 8).The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, and Safety Data Sheets (SDS) are on site (photos 14-16). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Well 1H is equipped with a well tag (photos 12 and 13). Three additional gas wells are on site that appear to be equipped for production (photo 11). The well and operator's information are displayed and visible on this well tag, as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h). No evidence of fluid leaks, such as staining, was observed on the ground around the gas wells. Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued against the spill reportedly discovered by the operator on 5/17/2026.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
Violation ID: 8271238
Permit API: 129-24171
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/17/2026
Comments: On April 17, 2026, the DEP conducted a FUI of Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc's Armstrong 2 gas well following IR4155454 where violations were continued for an inadequately stabilized shared and direct access road. Present during today's inspection is DEP ET Rosie Wise.A NOV response has yet to be received from the operator of this gas well following IR3891447 when viols were issued however, the DEP has been in communication with the other operator who utilizes the shared portion of the access road. IR4155472 documents the other operator stating they would visit the site to assess the shared road. Observations collected of the shared access road during IR 4155454 include deep erosion rills with water actively flowing down the access road and an exposed and cracked open culvert pipe. During IR 4155454, the DEP requested the operator(s) provide the DEP with a written timeline of remedial actions to repair the access road. To date, this written timeline this has yet to be received. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the shared portion of the access road (Wildcat Road) to be graded with all erosion rills and the exposed culvert pipe removed. Dirt that appeared to be removed from the road during grading was observed to be piled up along the right side of the shared access road. Clumps of this dirt was also observed in the floodway/streambank of a stream located directly downslope and to the right of the shared access road. The broken culvert pipe was observed to be lying on the ground adjacent to the access road, another piece of culvert piping that the broken piece was connected to was still observed to be in the ground and partially buried. Water was not observed to be actively discharging out of this culvert outlet as it appears the inlet may be blocked and resulting in seepage of water along other portions of the access road downslope. The DEP notes that no E and S controls appeared to be installed anywhere along the shared access road. Violations are being issued at this time for sediment entering the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC) and for failure to install E and S controls during earth disturbance activity.At the time of this inspection, no other active E and S issues were observed along the shared portions of Wildcat Road, however, the shared road was not stabilized with gravel and is exhibiting the potential for other E and S issues to occur.The DEP recommends the Operator remove the sediment from the WOC, stabilize the access road, unblock/replace the culvert pipe and install E and S controls along the access road to prevent any further e and s issues.Upon inspection of the direct portion of the access road, conditions appear to be unchanged, the DEP observed large areas of the access road to be flooded. An exposed pipe was observed alongside the access road, however no methane or other odor was detected, the exposed portion of the pipe did not appear to be compromised.At the time of this inspection, the gas well site was still observed to be overgrown with vegetation. A well tag with all required information posted on it was observed to be fixed to a heavily rusted wellhead. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the gas wellhead or other production equipment on site at this time, however, a strong gas odor and hissing sound was observed to be coming from the lower portion of the gas wellhead. OGI assistance is being requested at this time to assess the gas wellhead for a gas release. Refer to IR 4183514 for the continuation of violations for heavily rusted production equipment.While onsite, the DEP called the number on the well tag in an attempt to notify the operator of the new violations, however, the number was not in service. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for an inadequately stabilized access road are being continued, and new violations are being issued for sediment entering WOC and failure to implement E and S controls.

Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). As part of remediating the third area, due diligence should be given to establish the source of the product and any potential subsurface connection to the riser.

There are no signs of recent excavation in this area, there is no apparent surface connection between this area and the prior two.These observations indicate a recent partial cleanup of a crude oil release from the riser. Additional cleanup measures will be required throughout the area near the riser and northwest of the riser in order for those areas to be considered sufficiently remediated. As part of remediating the third area, due diligence should be given to establish the source of the product and any potential subsurface connection to the riser.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/13/2022 to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Cogan House Twp, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/13/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 961489
Permit API: 081-20962
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/13/2022
Comments: On July 12, 2022, Range Resources Kirby Steck called DEP Brad Kline at 1430 to report that a water hauler was in the process of dewatering the production fluid tanks at the Porter Stephen Pad, when the hose from the water truck became obstructed and began leaking from an open bleeder valve of the truck. The bleeder valve leaked water outside of containment onto the well pad surface. Range Resources immediately mobilized equipment to the site to begin excavating the impacted soil. Mr. Steck called DEP at 1545 to update DEP on the removal of the impacted soil and to increase the estimate of the volume of production fluid spilled to approximately 2 barrels. On July 13, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection at the Range Resources Porter Stephen Well Pad in response to a reported spill (CTS 365470) of 2 barrels of produced fluid from a water tank truck. At the time of inspection, Range Resources had excavated and area approximately 20 ft. by 20 ft. with a narrow 10 ft. area extending south from the main excavation. The spill occurred next to the containment for the production fluid tanks. DEP screened the excavation area with a soil conductivity meter. The screening resulted in finding 3 small areas that were over range of the soil conductivity meter. These areas were shown to Range Resources Kirby Steck when he arrived on site. Mr. Steck began hand digging these area as I left the site. There were three covered roll off dumpsters onsite filled with impacted soil. Mr. Steck said Moody and Associates are scheduled to be onsite to begin the Act 2 sampling and assessment on July 14, 2022. The spill of production fluid outside of containment to the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301.
